prose: The AP Stylebook's guidance on AI language: artificial intelligence systems do not think, feel, want or understand, so avoid language that gives them human characteristics - anthropomorphizing, the habit of ascribing human traits, emotions or behaviors to non-human things.

The recommended alternative is functional description: explain what a system does, how well it performs, who built it and who could be affected by it. The guidance was posted alongside AP coverage of OpenAI flagging concerning model behavior.
highlights: AP Stylebook: avoid anthropomorphizing AI - systems do not think, feel, want or understand.
Anthropomorphizing defined as ascribing human traits to non-human things.
Recommended frame: what a system does, how well it performs, who built it, who is affected.
Posted alongside AP coverage of OpenAI flagging concerning model behavior.
